content:
emma: Heads-up — saw a cluster of users where the client reconnects after a soft socket close but receives duplicate SSE/WS events. Not consistent with normal resume flows.
raj: Which proxy path? edge LB or internal router?
emma: edge LB -> proxy pool -> runtime. Seems to happen right after deploy at ~12:22 UTC. Small % of connections.
maya: Logs show client got `1001` then reconnected and server replayed the last chunk. Might be our proxy not marking session as terminated before requeueing events.
liam: Could be due to soft-close behavior: proxy returns 200/empty on close, our shard thinks unacked frames need replay.
raj: Can you paste the trace id and a short log snippet?
emma: trace=trace-1a2b, snippet:
```
proxy: conn 0x7f3 - socket soft-close (code=1001)
proxy: requeue stream-id=st-345 -> runtime pool
runtime: shard 12 - replaying last-window for st-345
client: reconnect new session id=sess-87
runtime: emit events [evt-201..evt-206]
client: ack none (client reconnects too fast)
```
liam: Ah — the runtime replays because it doesn't see a final ack before proxy requeue. But if proxy soft-close was client-initiated, we must not replay.
maya: Right now our resume idempotency key is tied to session token + last-ack. If proxy requeues before ack update, runtime can't differentiate.
raj: Could we add a `soft_close_reason` header on proxy->runtime when requeuing? e.g., `x-proxy-close: client-initiated` vs `server-fatal` so runtime decides to skip replay.
liam: That helps routing logic but won't solve billing/quotas: replays currently count against token usage, double-billing risk.
maya: For quotas we can gate replayed tokens under a `replay_flag` tag and exclude from charge until client sends a stable ack. Need console to surface `replay_count` per trace.
emma: Console UX ask: show a rejoin/replay timeline on traces and an option to collapse replayed tokens from cost calc for a short window (10s).
raj: Implementation notes: proxy adds `x-proxy-close` and `x-proxy-requeue-ts`; runtime annotates replayed events with `replay=yes` and emits metric `stream.replay.count`.
liam: Also add a circuit-window to disallow automatic replay if reconnection happens within 250ms (likely client TCP race). Could reduce dupes.
maya: I'll sketch a patch: proxy header + runtime gating + metric + sampling flag that surfaces in console trace.
emma: +1. Also we need an incident alert rule to surface spikes in `stream.replay.count` vs `stream.disconnect.rate`.
oncall-bot: Alert: spike detected - stream.replay.count increased 4x in last 5m for service/runtime-us-east-1
raj: Good catch bot. For rollout: let's ship proxy header on canary only and instrument telemetry first, not change billing. We can evaluate after ~24h.
liam: Agree. Rollout plan: canary proxy header -> collect metrics for 6h -> enable runtime gating on canary -> 24h monitor -> opt-in billing exclusion.
maya: I'll open a PR with the proxy header patch and runtime metric tags. Assigning reviewers @raj @liam.
emma: Thx. Also update the console trace schema to include `replay: true/false` and a small tooltip explaining it.
raj: One more thought — downstream integrations (webhooks) may get duplicate events too; add a webhook dedupe TTL header so consumers can dedupe if needed.
liam: Good call.
emma: filing a follow-up doc for webhook dedupe options.
raj: OK, prioritize telemetry so SRE can decide billing treatment.
maya: PR: github.com/redwood/proxy/pull/734
liam: I'll prepare runtime canary config.
emma: Thanks all. I'll update the oncall playbook with a short runbook: if `stream.replay.count` > 3x baseline, flip canary to rollback. :thumbsup:
